fields.meta_title: Occupational Therapy Intake Form Builder | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build an occupational therapy intake form that asks which daily tasks are hard and saves every answer to a database you own. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build an Occupational Therapy Intake Form Around Daily Tasks
fields.hero_description: Build an occupational therapy intake form that records the daily tasks each patient wants back, in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What the Therapist Knows Before the Evaluation
fields.features_subheading: Describe your caseload, and Emergent builds an occupational therapy intake form around the daily tasks patients want to get back.
fields.feature_1:
Daily tasks the patient marks as hard

Give patients a checklist of daily tasks such as getting dressed, cooking, writing, and opening jars. They tick the hard ones, and the therapist starts the evaluation there.
fields.feature_2:
Injured hand and writing hand, asked apart

Ask about the injured hand and the hand the patient writes with as separate questions. When both answers name the same hand, a Dominant hand label sits at the top of the chart.
fields.feature_3:
Pediatric sections that follow the child's age

A parent enters the child's age first. School questions about the grade and the teacher's main concern appear only for children 5 and older, and younger ones skip them.
fields.feature_4:
Goals the patient rates from 1 to 10

Patients name the activities they most want back and rate how well they manage each one from 1 to 10. The same goals return at re-evaluation, and both ratings sit side by side.
fields.feature_5:
A front desk list for missing referrals

Ask for the referring physician on every intake. An intake that arrives with that field blank goes to a front desk list, so staff can call the patient before anything is booked.
fields.feature_6:
The codebase in your GitHub repository

On paid plans, export the code for the intake form and its chart screens to your GitHub repository. A developer can host it on the clinic's own servers and keep building on it.

fields.usecase_heading: Where the Answers Go in Four OT Practices
fields.tab_content_1:
Every child 5 or older gets school questions

Fernwold Pediatric Therapy asks each parent for the child's age first. Bettina Ellingboe enters 7 for her son Soren, and the school section opens. She ticks buttons and zippers as hard at home, picks 2nd grade, and types handwriting as the teacher's main concern. Wilhelmina Mwale reads it all before his evaluation.
fields.tab_content_2:
A label when the injured hand is the writing hand

Hollybank Hand Therapy asks every new patient two questions: which hand was injured, and which hand they write with. When the injured hand is the writing hand, the chart gets a Dominant hand label. Lorcan Osei-Bonsu answers left to both, and Henrike Ravindran sees the label before his 2:15 evaluation.
fields.tab_content_3:
No referral on the intake, no slot on the calendar

Pinmoor Driver Rehab books a driving evaluation only when the intake names a referring physician. The form also asks for license status and when the patient last drove. Thaddeus Ellwood fills in both but leaves the physician blank. His intake goes to Saoirse Kowal's front desk list, and she calls him for the name.
fields.tab_content_4:
By week 8, all four goals are rated again

Hartsmere Occupational Therapy asks new patients for the activities that matter most, each rated from 1 to 10. Philippa Northcote picks cooking dinner, gardening, typing emails, and carrying groceries, at 3, 2, 4, and 5. At week 8 she rates the same four again: 7, 6, 8, and 7. Ngozi Petrakis sees both columns side by side.

fields.hero_prompt: Build an occupational therapy intake form for my outpatient clinic that asks new patients which daily tasks are hard right now.

faq_plan.q: What is an occupational therapy intake form?
How do I create an occupational therapy intake form?

plan.angle: The SERP for this query has no top 10 in the workbook, and the AlsoAsked tree drifts into OT careers and autism therapy. Generic intake templates ask for a diagnosis and stop. This page wins by building the intake around what occupational therapy treats: the daily tasks a patient cannot do now, which hand is injured and which one writes, age-based pediatric sections, a referral check for driving evaluations, and goals the patient rates from 1 to 10 and rates again at re-evaluation.
tab_stories: Bettina Ellingboe enters age 7 for her son Soren on the Fernwold Pediatric Therapy intake, the school section for children 5 and older opens, and Wilhelmina Mwale reads his 2nd grade teacher's handwriting concern before the evaluation.

Lorcan Osei-Bonsu answers left for the injured hand and left for the writing hand on the Hollybank Hand Therapy intake, and Henrike Ravindran sees a Dominant hand label on his chart before his 2:15 evaluation.

Thaddeus Ellwood leaves the referring physician blank on the Kilnworth Driver Rehab intake, the clinic books driving evaluations only with a referral, and his intake waits on Saoirse Kowal's front desk list until she calls him.
Philippa Northcote rates 4 goals at intake at Hartsmere Occupational Therapy (3, 2, 4, and 5 out of 10) and again at week 8 (7, 6, 8, and 7), and Ngozi Petrakis sees both columns side by side.
